rows.answer: The documents do not specify what share of a traffic cone's weight must be in its base. The MUTCD guidance only states that ballast should be kept to the minimum amount needed and that cones may be doubled up or have weighted bases or sandbag rings for stability [1]. For abandoning a pipe in NCDOT right of way, the pipe must be filled with grout or flowable fill to at least 90 percent full, or completely full when on railroad right of way [2].

Mobile work may stop for up to 5 minutes at a time [1]. Under standard placement in the Utilities Accommodation Manual, a street light pole must be placed 5 feet 6 inches behind the face of the guardrail [2].

**The documents give different values:**
- Division, NCDOT Maintenance/Utility Traffic Control Guidelines (MUTCG), Chapter 5: Work Operations / Construction & Maintenance Activities: 5 minutes [1]
- Federal, Work Zone Operations Best Practices Guidebook, Third Edition (FHWA-HOP-13-012, 2013): 15 minutes [3]
- State, Utilities Accommodation Manual, Version 2.0 (July 2022): 5 feet 6 inches [2]
- Federal, Highway/Utility Guide (FHWA-SA-93-049, June 1993): 3.5 feet [4]

**Recommendation** (the assistant's judgment, not an NCDOT rule): For mobile work stoppage duration, follow the NCDOT MUTCG value of 5 minutes [1] because it is the current state guideline that defines the Mobile category, whereas the 15-minute figure in the FHWA guidebook [3] describes an older version of NCDOT's definitions. For street light pole placement behind guardrail, follow the NCDOT Utilities Accommodation Manual value of 5 feet 6 inches [2] as it is the current state standard for pole placement, while the 3.5-foot value in the 1993 FHWA Highway/Utility Guide [4] is an older federal reference.

Per the MUTCD notes for Figure 6P-2, the signing shown shall be used whenever blasting caps are used within 1,000 feet of a roadway [1]. Under the Utilities Accommodation Manual, for a utility to have a compensable interest by adverse possession, possession must have begun 20 years prior to the facilities being taken into NCDOT right of way [2].

**The documents give different values:**
- State, NCDOT 2024 Roadway Standard Drawings, Division 11: Work Zone Traffic Control (combined): 1,000' [3]
- Federal, MUTCD 11th Edition (December 2023), Part 6: Temporary Traffic Control: 1,000 feet [1]
- State, Utilities Accommodation Manual, Version 2.0 (July 2022): 20 years [2]
- Division, NCDOT Utility Cost Reimbursement Guidance (Aug 20, 2026): 20 years (without color of title) [4]
- Internal, NCDOT Utilities Coordination and Encroachments Webinar, slides with speaker notes (Aug 2017): 20 years [5]

**Recommendation** (the assistant's judgment, not an NCDOT rule): For the blasting zone signing distance, both the federal MUTCD 11th Edition (passage 3) and the NCDOT Roadway Standard Drawings (passage 1) specify 1,000 feet, so they are consistent. For the adverse possession period, the Utilities Accommodation Manual (passage 5) states the governing statutory requirement of 20 years prior to facilities being taken into NCDOT right of way, which is also reflected in the Utility Cost Reimbursement Guidance (passage 7) and the 2017 webinar (passage 8); the UAM is the current authoritative manual for compensable interest determinations.

The MUTCD lists the End Work Zone Speed Limit (R2‑12) sign as 36 × 54 inches for freeway or expressway installations [1]. The July 7 2010 Chief Engineer memo requires any alternate specialty fence on control‑of‑access limits to meet a minimum height of 48 inches [2].

**Recommendation** (the assistant's judgment, not an NCDOT rule): Check both documents; neither value is shown as the one to follow.

Per the Utilities Accommodation Manual, when guardrail post spacing is reduced to 3 ft 1.5 in., a light pole may be placed 3 ft 6 in. behind the face of the guardrail [1]. In the Work Zone Traffic Control Design Manual, Detail 3‑2A (Run‑out Length table) shows that for a design speed of 60 mph and an ADT of 800–2,000 vpd the run‑out length LR is 345 ft [2].

**The documents give different values:**
- Division, Work Zone Traffic Control Design Manual (TMP Design Manual): 345 ft [2]
- State, Utilities Accommodation Manual, Version 2.0 (July 2022): 3 feet 6 inches [1]
- Federal, Highway/Utility Guide (FHWA-SA-93-049, June 1993): 3.5 feet [3]

**Recommendation** (the assistant's judgment, not an NCDOT rule): For guardrail post spacing reduced to 3 feet 1.5 inches, the Utilities Accommodation Manual (UAM) specifies 3 feet 6 inches behind the face of guardrail [1], which is the governing state standard for utility accommodation. The Federal Highway/Utility Guide recommends 3.5 feet (3 feet 6 inches) as a minimum for guardrail function [3], which aligns with the UAM value. For runout length LR at 60 mph with ADT 800–2,000, the Work Zone Traffic Control Design Manual provides 345 ft [2]; the Roadway Design Manual references Detail 3-2A for LR but does not include the table in the provided passages …

**The documents give different values:**

**Recommendation** (the assistant's judgment, not an NCDOT rule): Follow the NCDOT Utilities Accommodation Manual's 5 feet 6 inches requirement because it is the current state standard (July 2022) that specifically governs utility accommodations on North Carolina highways, whereas the federal guide's 3.5 feet is from a 1993 document that provides general guidance rather than state-specific requirements.

Where a guardrail is present, poles shall be placed 5 feet 6 inches behind the face of the guard rail under standard placement [1].

**The documents give different values:**
- State, Utilities Accommodation Manual, Version 2.0 (July 2022): 5 feet 6 inches behind the face of the guard rail [1]
- Federal, Highway/Utility Guide (FHWA-SA-93-049, June 1993): 3.5 feet from face of guardrail to face of utility object [2]

**Recommendation** (the assistant's judgment, not an NCDOT rule): Follow the Utilities Accommodation Manual's 5 feet 6 inches requirement because it is the current NCDOT state manual (July 2022) specifically governing utility pole placement, whereas the federal guide's 3.5 feet is from a 1993 publication and the UAM explicitly states its setback requirements in Section 3.3.3 and details the guardrail placement rule in Section 3.3.7.9 [1].

Standard placement may be reduced to 3 feet 6 inches behind the face of the guardrail when the spacing for guardrail posts is reduced to 3 feet 1.5 inches [1].

**The documents give different values:**
- State, Utilities Accommodation Manual, Version 2.0 (July 2022): 3 feet 6 inches [1]
- Federal, Highway/Utility Guide (FHWA-SA-93-049, June 1993): 3.5 feet [2]

**Recommendation** (the assistant's judgment, not an NCDOT rule): The Utilities Accommodation Manual (UAM) is the governing North Carolina state document for utility accommodations and specifically addresses the reduced guardrail post spacing of 3 feet 1.5 inches, allowing a reduced setback of 3 feet 6 inches behind the face of the guardrail [1]. The Federal Highway/Utility Guide provides a general minimum of 3.5 feet (3 feet 6 inches) for guardrail-to-utility-object clearance but does not reference the specific post-spacing condition [2]. For projects under NCDOT jurisdiction, the UAM value should be followed.
